entries.exact_span: وهو العاص بن وائل . وكانت العرب تسمي من كان له بنون وبنات ، ثم مات البنون وبقي البنات : أبتر . فيقال : إن العاص وقف مع النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - يكلمه ، فقال له جمع من صناديد قريش : مع من كنت واقفا ؟ فقال : مع ذلك الأبتر . وكان قد توفي قبل ذلك عبد الله ابن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ، وكان من خديجة ;

and he is al-'As ibn Wa'il. The Arabs used to call the one who had sons and daughters, then the sons died while the daughters remained, "abtar" (cut off). It is said that al-'As stood with the Prophet—may Allah's prayers and peace be upon him—speaking with him, when a group of the chiefs of Quraysh said to him: "With whom were you standing?" He said: "With that abtar one." And 'Abdullah, the son of the Messenger of Allah—may Allah's prayers and peace be upon him—had died before this, and he was from Khadijah.

analysis.opening_assertion_en: and he is al-'As ibn Wa'il.
analysis.finding: The stored pair separates Qurtubi's stated identification of the referent from an unnamed event-report about him. The English keeps the passive/anonymous formula; it does not add a narrator or route.

sources.locator: Qurtubi on 108:3, paragraph beginning أي مبغضك ; وهو العاص بن وائل and next sentence فيقال.
sources.supports: Exact anonymous reporting marker and event span.

sources.supports: Parallel display of anonymous formula, referent, and event details.

sources.locator: Asbab al-Nuzul, Surah al-Kawthar, parallel reports beginning قال ابن عباس and وقال عطاء عن ابن عباس.

sources.locator: Tafsir Ibn Kathir, 108:3, Muhammad ibn Ishaq from Yazid ibn Ruman.
sources.supports: A different named report route; not imported into Qurtubi.

source_boundary: The al-As identification before فيقال is not an attribution for who transmitted the following event report. Dialog speakers are narrative participants, not transmitters. Parallel attributions from al-Wahidi or Ibn Kathir cannot fill Qurtubi's absent route.
